newsitem.title: LEBANON: Beirut banks trade at record highs. [CORRECTED 12:50 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Beirut banks trade at record highs. [CORRECTED 12:50 GMT]

text.p: Bank shares traded at record highs on the Beirut Stock Exchange on Monday while Solidere shares continued to slide in profit-taking.
The LIBX bank index climbed 1.67 percent to 188.44. The BLOM general index dropped 3.83 percent to 1059.50 and the LISPI general index fell 0.45 percent to 94.76.
Banque Libanais pour le Commerce rose 4.8 percent to a new high of $22.5 from $21.5. Banque Audi also hit a record $28.75 from $28.6250 while Bank of Beirut maintained the $4.6875 level.
"I think BLC has the highest potential for investors right now," Nicholas Sawan of Lebanon Invest told Reuters.
He said the price/earnings ratios for Lebanese banks were heading toward 18. They currently range between 14 and 16.
"In two months' time investors will be looking at 1998 earnings forecasts. Banks' growth is expected to be strong next year," Sawan said.
However, some other financial analysts have been less optimistic about future bank profits because of pressure on interest margins.
Solidere A and B shares dropped to $12.25 (corrects from $12.5) from $12.8750 on Friday. Last Tuesday, the shares hit a two-year record price of $13.75.
"It is still a period of profit-taking. Solidere shares could trade in the coming few months between the high $11 and the high $13 area," Sawan said.
BSE turnover rose to 307,715 from 291,908 shares for a value of $3,946,694 against $3,519,732.
There was no trade in the other three listed industrial firms -- Ciments Blanc, Eternit and Uniceramic.
